title: Israel certifies election result, rejecting Netanyahu's fraud claims, as Herzog starts talks
dek: The election committee says an audit of 9,069 polling stations found nothing that harmed the vote. The first two parties to meet the president back Netanyahu, but the opposition expects more endorsements for Gadi Eisenkot.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Israel's Central Elections Committee on Wednesday certified the result of the 27 October parliamentary election and said it had found no evidence of fraud. That rejects claims, pushed by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party, that Arab-led parties "stole" the vote. President Isaac Herzog accepted the certified results as legally binding and began meeting parties that evening to decide who gets the first chance to form a government.

The committee said it had audited 9,069 polling stations after complaints and was confident the results "accurately reflect the will of the voters", reports said. "All complaints submitted by political factions have been reviewed and there were no findings indicating harm to the integrity of the election," the committee said in its statement. Neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition camp led by former army chief Gadi Eisenkot has the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member Knesset.

## What happened

The committee's chairman, Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, presented the final results to Herzog at the President's Residence in Jerusalem at noon (3:30 pm IST). He said it was dangerous to cast doubt on results that are legally binding, reports said. Public trust in the electoral process is "easy to destroy, yet very difficult to repair", he said.

Sohlberg also addressed a separate inquiry by the Shin Bet, Israel's domestic security service, into alleged foreign interference. In a closed meeting of committee members on Wednesday he read out a Shin Bet assessment describing a "widespread phenomenon involving the influx of substantial funds into Israel from foreign states", according to a transcript obtained by one news agency. The Shin Bet gave no evidence for the assertion, the agency said. Sohlberg said in public that these were "merely suspicions" and that even if they were proven, "the scope of their potential impact is limited". One report said that the suspicions concern money said to have come from countries such as Qatar and Turkey to influence voting in Arab communities.

On Tuesday Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara had refused the Shin Bet's request to question several elected Arab lawmakers, including Ra'am leader Mansour Abbas, Israeli media reported. "It is not permissible to interrogate citizens or elected officials without evidence to justify such action," she said. Likud accused her of trying to "obstruct the investigation". The Shin Bet is headed by David Zini, whom Netanyahu appointed.

Herzog's consultations began on Wednesday evening, after a delay caused by a security alert at the residence that brought police bomb-disposal teams, reports said. The far-right Religious Zionist Party, led by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, and the ultra-Orthodox Shas party, led by Arye Deri, each with six seats, recommended Netanyahu. Shas's representative said Netanyahu "will know how" to build a coalition, one report said. The talks continue through Thursday evening.

## The numbers

Final results as reported:

- 120 seats in the Knesset; 61 needed for a majority
- 53 for Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc
- 48 for the opposition camp around Eisenkot
- 19 for the Arab-led lists, the Joint List and Ra'am, a record
- 11 parties in the new Knesset

According to one report, Eisenkot is expected to receive 48 recommendations and Netanyahu 46, with United Torah Judaism expected to back neither. Another report said that the Joint List and Ra'am are expected to recommend Eisenkot. If all 19 Arab-led seats did so, Eisenkot would have the support of 67 members, a majority of the house, though that would not by itself give him a governing coalition.

## Background

Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, has repeatedly alleged that the Arab-majority parties won through fraud, pointing to election-day arrests of people carrying envelopes of cash and later saying lawmakers had received money from Qatar, reports said. The election committee, the police and the committee's acting director general have all said there is no basis for the claim that the election was stolen. Netanyahu has called for a "broad national government" under his leadership. He is on trial on corruption charges, which he denies.

On Tuesday, Eisenkot, Naftali Bennett, Yair Lapid, Yair Golan and Avigdor Liberman agreed to recommend Eisenkot as prime minister and said they would not form a coalition with the Arab-led parties. That leaves them short of a majority unless they win over parties from Netanyahu's side or rely on Arab-led support from outside the government.

## What they are saying

Likud accused Eisenkot, Bennett, Lapid and Liberman of planning "a dangerous government relying on terror supporters", one report said, and Netanyahu's supporters rallied in Tel Aviv against any government that depends on Arab parties.

Eisenkot accused Likud of attempting a "pogrom against democracy", reports said. Lapid said the Shin Bet "outbursts", together with the Democratic wins in Tuesday's US midterm elections, "eliminate any possibility of a unity government led by Netanyahu". Golan accused Netanyahu of refusing to recognise the result, one report said.

## What happens next

Herzog is not legally required to pick the candidate with the most endorsements. When the consultations end, he will ask a member of the Knesset, most likely Netanyahu or Eisenkot, to try to form a government. That person has 28 days, which can be extended by 14. If no one succeeds, Israel would hold another election early next year. Herzog has said he wants "creative solutions" to avoid that, and reports said that his remarks have raised speculation he could sound out leaders on a unity government. The new Knesset is sworn in on 10 November.

## Why it matters for India

India has close defence, technology and trade ties with Israel, which is also part of the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor that New Delhi has promoted since 2023. Israel's next government will set policy on the stalled Gaza ceasefire and on Iran. Eisenkot has warned Netanyahu against starting a new war against Iran alongside the US, reports said. A wider war would matter directly for India, whose oil imports and seafarers depend on the Strait of Hormuz.
